headlines.influence: Negative headlines are the source of the fear extreme, which the CAG treats as contrarian bullish. They add downside gap risk but are not used as a bearish signal.

options_flow.influence: The bearish headline P/C is discounted as hedging because multileg share is very high and ISO share is very low. The net effect is mildly offsetting.

gex.values_cited: Net GEX -$590M, flip 6290, put wall 6900, call wall 7000, spot 6948.77
gex.influence: Spot is bracketed by the walls, which defines the targets (SPY ~$690 to ~$700). Negative GEX amplifies moves, so I widen ranges 2x.

vix_structure.influence: Backwardation confirms stress but also marks capitulation-style fear. Supports the trend-following explosive-regime playbook with a bullish-only bias.

vol_regime.values_cited: EXPLOSIVE regime, confidence 40%, backtested 65.5% accuracy (bullish only), CAG 2.44 BULL-DELUDED with Fear z=+3.79
vol_regime.influence: Highest weight: the regime rule is bullish only, and the CAG gives the contrarian edge. Confidence is held low because regime confidence is only 40%.

signal_attribution.reasoning_chain: Negative GEX (-$590M) with VIX backwardation puts the market in the EXPLOSIVE regime, the best backtested regime and bullish-only. Headline and put flow look bearish, but SPX/SPXW is 88-92% multileg hedging with ISO under 1.2%, so it does not confirm downside conviction. CAG of +2.44 with Fear z=+3.79 adds a contrarian bullish edge, and spot sits above the 6900 put wall. Result: a low-confidence BULLISH intraday and next-day call (40-42%) with 2x ranges and a medium-confidence 30-day call (58%), anchored on the 6900/7000 walls.
